body.statement:
For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the bounded rational-table search on a nonzero-normal-form branch of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) contains at most
\[
 2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
coordinate descriptions. Every candidate test is decidable by exact rational arithmetic. Whenever the search returns \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\), one has \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and, for at least one outcome cell \(y\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger});
\]
hence the two represented DAG intervention vectors differ.
body.proof_tex:
An integer of bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) has at most \(2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}\) signed descriptions under the fixed encoding. Describing one reduced rational coordinate by a signed numerator and a positive denominator therefore uses at most
\[
 2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
pairs. Taking the Cartesian product over the \(m\) cells gives at most
\[
 \left(2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\right)^m
 =2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
table descriptions. Positivity and normalization, coprimality, and duplicate removal can only decrease this number.

For a rational candidate, normalization, cell positivity, all oracle-one polynomial equalities, every oracle-zero strict sum-of-squares inequality, every recorded denominator, and every signature are decidable by exact integer arithmetic after clearing positive denominators. Thus the membership and failed-signature tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\) are exact.

If the procedure returns \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\), its return test gives
\[
 p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega},
 \qquad F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\neq0
\]
for some \(y\). As in the proof of equality-branch soundness, strict positivity and \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) imply
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})>0.
\]
The cross-signature definition then yields
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})-T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})}
 {B_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})}\neq0.
\]
One unequal coordinate makes the two intervention vectors unequal, proving soundness of every returned separator and the stated finite-search bound.
